method: Read the two official Google Search Central pages and compared the claims below with their relevant passages. No live index-removal experiment was run.
claim_origin: Editor-constructed statements for a source-checking exercise; not an observed AI response.

claims.claim: Blocking a web page in robots.txt guarantees it will not appear in Google Search.
claims.section: What is a robots.txt file used for? — Web page
claims.supporting_excerpt: its URL can still appear in search results
claims.decision: Replace the guarantee: robots.txt controls crawling; a blocked page URL may still appear in Google Search.

claims.claim: Googlebot must be able to access a page to read its noindex rule.
claims.section: Block Search indexing with noindex — Important
claims.supporting_excerpt: the page or resource must not be blocked by a robots.txt file
claims.decision: Keep the crawl-access condition when explaining noindex.

claims.claim: A specific URL will disappear from results tomorrow after noindex is added.
claims.decision: Do not promise a date; the documentation does not establish the recrawl or removal time of a particular URL.

not_established: Any specific URL's current indexing status
